newsitem.title: INDIA: Hopes of political compromise buoy Bombay shares.
newsitem.headline: Hopes of political compromise buoy Bombay shares.

text.p: Bombay stocks rallied strongly on Wednesday, encouraged by optimism that talks between the government and its erstwhile Congress ally will defuse a political crisis, traders and analysts said.
"The market is really sensitive to political developments taking place in New Delhi," said Piyush Vora, a member-broker of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
The BSE's benchmark 30-share index surged 131.80 points, or 3.74 percent, to end at a provisional 3,652.29 close.
The ruling United Front alliance and Congress party, which withdrew support for the minority coalition 11 days ago, were due to begin talks on Wednesday to try to resolve the dispute.
But, nagging fears ahead of a confidence vote set for Friday will restrict strong buying, analysts said.
"Foreign funds have to buy at some level of certainty," said Ramdeo Agarwal, research head at Motilal Oswal Securities.
A swift resolution to the drama would mean a market-friendly 1997/98 budget will be left intact, analysts said.
"Everybody is waiting for the vote. We expect the market to go up substantially if the budget is passed," said Tushar Sarda, president and chief executive at Daewoo Securities.
The budget proposals unveiled on February 28 slash corporate and personal taxes, lower import tariffs and legalise company share buy-backs.
"Broadly, we are back to the same levels when the crisis started," Sandeep Dhingra, equity analyst at SSKI Securities, told Reuters on Wednesday.
The budget had been expected to be passed on April 21. There is now no indication as to when a budget vote can be taken.
The Bombay index crashed over eight percent after the Congress announcement, but has since then recovered.
